analysis_document.title: Hello-World External Fixture Analysis
analysis_document.subtitle: Decision-oriented report for a pinned one-line README repository.
analysis_document.source_basis: Authored from the complete included source inventory of the pinned external repository: README line 1.

open_questions.question: Is this repository intended only as a greeting fixture, or should it grow into a maintained example with tests and release ownership?
open_questions.reason: The only source evidence is a one-line README, so intended ownership and future use cannot be proven from source.
open_questions.impact: This affects whether the right next action is to keep the repository tiny or add project structure.
open_questions.evidence_gap: No contributing, license, tests, runtime source or project documentation are present in the included inventory.

executive_decision_basis.summary: This pinned external repository is a one-line Hello World fixture, not evidence of a running product system.
executive_decision_basis.recommendation: Keep it tiny if the goal is a fixture; add explicit project structure only if the owner expects it to become a maintained example.
executive_decision_basis.confidence: high for the README-only scope, low for any product behavior beyond that line.

decision_questions.keep_system: Keep as a minimal greeting fixture when the desired outcome is only a tiny external smoke source.
decision_questions.modernize_system: Modernize only by adding ownership, license, test and usage documents if this is meant to become a maintained example.
decision_questions.replace_system: Replacement is not a meaningful decision from the source evidence; there is no implemented system to replace.
decision_questions.cost: Expected cost is negligible for keeping the fixture and small for adding basic repository hygiene.
decision_questions.biggest_risks: The main risk is overinterpreting a one-line README as proof of behavior, architecture, process or security.
decision_questions.next_actions: Confirm owner intent, then either leave the repository unchanged or add minimal project metadata.

consistency_review.summary: The report consistently treats README line 1 as the only proven source fact and marks unsupported product dimensions as partial or open.

skill_workbench_synthesis.summary: No skill workbenches were planned or executed because the strategy found only a one-line README fixture.
skill_workbench_synthesis.coverage_statement: The report integrates the explicit no-skill decision from the analysis strategy.

detail_review_synthesis.summary: No detail reviews were planned or executed because no runtime, contract, test or configuration source exists.
detail_review_synthesis.coverage_statement: The final report integrates the pre-final detail plan's skip decision.

sections.title: Executive Decision
sections.intent: Answer the decision question without inflating the repository.

blocks.title: Decision Summary
paragraphs: README line 1 says "Hello World!". That is enough to classify this pinned external repository as a tiny greeting fixture, but not enough to claim runtime behavior, interfaces, architecture or delivery process.
The practical decision is simple: keep it as a fixture if that is the goal, or add basic project metadata only if the owner expects it to become a maintained example.

rows.recommendation: Keep the repository tiny unless owner intent says it should become a maintained example.
rows.risk: The main risk is readers assuming more behavior exists than the source supports.
